key_insight: The K/Rb–SnGeX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) lead-free double perovskite family is thermodynamically stable, mechanically ductile, and composition-tunable from wide-gap photovoltaic absorbers to high-ZT thermoelectric materials.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer an environmentally safer alternative to lead halide perovskites for solar, photodetection, and waste-heat recovery devices, with bandgaps and transport properties adjustable by halogen selection.
method: DFT-based study of structure, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties.
Calculated formation energies, tolerance factors, and octahedral factors to assess stability.
Derived elastic constants, band structures, effective masses, and ZT-related transport indicators.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV and a peak thermoelectric performance of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The most compelling thermoelectric result is reported at very high temperature, so experimental validation of phase stability and performance under operating conditions is still needed.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
